title: A Conversation With a Dogecoin Millionaire: An Update

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》负责商业和政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上，现场采访几位商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 扎伊尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，您可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Hey, it's Michael.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是迈克尔。

sentences.en: This week, The Daily is revisiting some of our favorite episodes of the year and hearing what's happened in the time since they first ran.
sentences.zh: 本周，《每日新闻》将重温我们今年最喜欢的一些节目，并了解它们首次播出后发生的事情。

sentences.en: Today, we return to the unlikely story of a 33-year-old who bought a cryptocurrency intended to be a meme and became a millionaire in the process
sentences.zh: 今天，我们回到那个不可思议的故事：一位33岁的年轻人买了一种本意是迷因的加密货币，并在此过程中成为了百万富翁，

sentences.en: to find out what he's lost or gained in the time since.
sentences.zh: 来看看他在这段时间里失去了什么，又得到了什么。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, December 29th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月29日，星期三。

sentences.en: So, Kevin, the last time we spoke with you, you had quite improbably made $750,000 by selling a picture of your column in the form of a non-fungible token.
sentences.zh: 那么，凯文，上次我们和你交谈时，你非常不可思议地通过以非同质化代币（NFT）的形式出售你的专栏图片赚了75万美元。

sentences.en: So, what have you been up to since then?
sentences.zh: 那么，从那以后你都在忙些什么呢？

sentences.en: Well, quick update.
sentences.zh: 嗯，简单更新一下。

sentences.en: The value of cryptocurrency has skyrocketed in the time since that episode.
sentences.zh: 自那期节目播出以来，加密货币的价值已经飞涨。

sentences.en: So, the NFT that I sold is actually now worth about $1.4 million.
sentences.zh: 所以我卖掉的那个NFT现在价值约140万美元。

sentences.en: Show off.
sentences.zh: 炫耀狂。

sentences.en: Again, I don't get to keep it.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我没能留住它。

sentences.en: I am a fake cryptocurrency millionaire, but there you go.
sentences.zh: 我是一个虚假的加密货币百万富翁，但事实就是这样。

sentences.en: So, I've kind of moved on from NFTs, but I've stayed very interested in the world of cryptocurrency.
sentences.zh: 所以，我算是已经不再关注NFT了，但我对加密货币的世界依然非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And for the last few weeks, there's been one giant story in the world of cryptocurrency, and that is the story of Dogecoin.
sentences.zh: 在过去几周里，加密货币世界发生了一件大事，那就是狗狗币的故事。

sentences.en: We're going to take Dogecoin to the moon.
sentences.zh: 我们要把狗狗币送上月球。

sentences.en: A positively dogged rise, it says here, in the price of Dogecoin.
sentences.zh: 这里写着，狗狗币的价格出现了积极的猛涨。

sentences.en: Dogecoin has been everywhere.
sentences.zh: 狗狗币无处不在。

sentences.en: Its total value stands at $86 billion, more than FedEx.
sentences.zh: 它的总价值达到了860亿美元，超过了联邦快递。

sentences.en: Every time I open my TikTok feed, there's like a video about Dogecoin.
sentences.zh: 我每次打开TikTok，都会看到关于狗狗币的视频。

sentences.en: Hold it, hold it, hold it, hold it, never sell.
sentences.zh: 拿着，拿着，拿着，拿着，永远别卖。

sentences.en: Much rich.
sentences.zh: 太富有了。

sentences.en: Buy more, buy more, buy more, buy more.
sentences.zh: 多买点，多买点，多买点，多买点。

sentences.en: It's doing well.
sentences.zh: 它表现得很好。

sentences.en: Every time I go on Twitter, there are people talking about it.
sentences.zh: 我每次上Twitter，都有人在谈论它。

sentences.en: I have friends that I haven't talked to in years, like texting me about whether or not they should invest in it.
sentences.zh: 我有好几年没联系的朋友，都在发短信问我是否应该投资它。

sentences.en: Every day, the internet has a main character.
sentences.zh: 每一天，互联网都有一个主角。

sentences.en: And today, you know,
sentences.zh: 而今天，你知道，

sentences.en: Reddit and Twitter have decided that main character is Dogecoin.
sentences.zh: Reddit和Twitter已经认定那个主角就是狗狗币。

sentences.en: So unlock that word and that concept for us, as only you can, Dogecoin.
sentences.zh: 那么，请像你擅长的那样，为我们解读一下“狗狗币”这个词和概念。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 没问题。

sentences.en: So Dogecoin is something like Bitcoin or Ethereum or Ethereum or any of these other cryptocurrencies.
sentences.zh: 狗狗币就像比特币、以太坊或任何其他加密货币一样。

sentences.en: It's a way to send and receive money on the internet.
sentences.zh: 它是一种在互联网上发送和接收资金的方式。

sentences.en: And it was created in 2013, during the first real speculative mania around Bitcoin.
sentences.zh: 它创建于2013年，是在围绕比特币的第一次真正的投机狂潮期间。

sentences.en: And it was literally meant as a joke.
sentences.zh: 而且它字面上就是作为一个笑话而创造的。

sentences.en: These two programmers created it to poke fun at how seriously all these investors and speculators were taking cryptocurrency.
sentences.zh: 这两位程序员创造它是为了嘲笑所有这些投资者和投机者对加密货币的认真态度。

sentences.en: And basically, they decided we should sort of make fun of the people trading cryptocurrencies by making our own joke cryptocurrency.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们决定通过制造我们自己的笑话加密货币，来嘲弄那些交易加密货币的人。

sentences.en: So they take this meme, this Shiba Inu dog, who was called Doge, that was sort of popular in the 2013 internet, who would like talk in like comic sans
sentences.zh: 所以他们采用了这个迷因，这只名叫“Doge”的柴犬，它在2013年的互联网上很流行，它会用Comic Sans字体说话，

sentences.en: and would say things like much wow, like so scare.
sentences.zh: 还会说像“太惊人”、“好害怕”之类的话。

sentences.en: So they decided we're going to combine Bitcoin with Doge and make Dogecoin.
sentences.zh: 所以他们决定把比特币和Doge结合起来，创造了狗狗币。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So given that context, who would bother to trade this parody of a currency, Dogecoin?
sentences.zh: 那么在这样的背景下，谁会费心去交易这种货币的戏仿品——狗狗币呢？

sentences.en: So for most of its life,
sentences.zh: 在它生命的大部分时间里，

sentences.en: Dogecoin is basically worthless.
sentences.zh: 狗狗币基本上是一文不值的。

sentences.en: One Dogecoin is worth a tiny fraction of a cent.
sentences.zh: 一个狗狗币只值几美分的一小部分。

sentences.en: But this year, as Bitcoin and Ethereum and these other cryptocurrencies are having another massive run,
sentences.zh: 但今年，随着比特币、以太坊和其他加密货币再次迎来大规模上涨，

sentences.en: Dogecoin made this very strange comeback.
sentences.zh: 狗狗币上演了这种非常奇怪的回归。

sentences.en: It totally exploded.
sentences.zh: 它彻底爆发了。

sentences.en: And I kept hearing about these big time Dogecoin traders.
sentences.zh: 我一直听说这些大牌狗狗币交易员的事。

sentences.en: There was one in particular, people on the Dogecoin subreddit were calling him like the Doge father or slum Doge millionaire.
sentences.zh: 其中有一个特别出名，狗狗币Reddit版块的人称他为“狗狗币之父”或“贫民窟狗狗币百万富翁”。

sentences.en: Would you mind just introducing yourself and explaining a little bit about who you are?
sentences.zh: 你介意自我介绍一下，并稍微解释一下你是谁吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, sure.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: And his name is Glauber Contesodo.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫格劳伯·孔特索多。

sentences.en: So I go by Jason or Pro, but my birth name is Glauber Contesodo.
sentences.zh: 我叫杰森或Pro，但我的出生名字是格劳伯·孔特索多。

sentences.en: We get on a video call.
sentences.zh: 我们进行了视频通话。

sentences.en: He's a big guy, big beard.
sentences.zh: 他是个大块头，留着大胡子。

sentences.en: He's got like a picture of Jay-Z behind him.
sentences.zh: 他身后有一张Jay-Z的照片。

sentences.en: And I work here in LA.
sentences.zh: 我在洛杉矶这里工作。

sentences.en: I work at a music company, a hip hop music company.
sentences.zh: 我在一家音乐公司工作，一家嘻哈音乐公司。

sentences.en: So Glauber is 33 years old.
sentences.zh: 格劳伯今年33岁。

sentences.en: He was born in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 他出生在巴西。

sentences.en: He came to the US when he was six years old and his family landed in the Washington DC area.
sentences.zh: 他六岁时来到美国，他的家人在华盛顿特区地区落脚。

sentences.en: We basically grew up very poor.
sentences.zh: 我们基本上是在非常贫困的环境中长大的。

sentences.en: So I remember growing up, we were in a little apartment, like basement kind of area.
sentences.zh: 我记得小时候，我们住在一个小公寓里，就像地下室那种地方。

sentences.en: I shared a room with my sister until I was like 13.
sentences.zh: 我和我姐姐共用一个房间，直到我13岁左右。

sentences.en: His mom and dad didn't even have their own room.
sentences.zh: 他的父母甚至没有自己的房间。

sentences.en: They had like the back end of the apartment that we had to like put a divider up so they had some privacy.
sentences.zh: 他们住在公寓的后半部分，我们不得不竖起隔板，这样他们才能有一点隐私。

sentences.en: So he graduates from high school, goes to college, but ends up dropping out and then stays in the DC area for a while.
sentences.zh: 他高中毕业后上了大学，但最终退学了，并在华盛顿特区地区待了一段时间。

sentences.en: And he meets this aspiring rapper and decides to manage him.
sentences.zh: 他遇到了一位有抱负的说唱歌手，并决定担任他的经纪人。

sentences.en: And like, he really wants to work in the music industry.
sentences.zh: 他真的很想在音乐行业工作。

sentences.en: Maryland is not the place for music.
sentences.zh: 马里兰州不是搞音乐的地方。

sentences.en: So I'm like, either I'm moving to New York or LA.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，要么搬到纽约，要么搬到洛杉矶。

sentences.en: I had some friends out here already.
sentences.zh: 我已经在那里有一些朋友了。

sentences.en: So I was like, LA it is.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，就去洛杉矶吧。

sentences.en: And like a lot of people who moved to LA hoping to have a career in the entertainment industry,
sentences.zh: 像许多搬到洛杉矶希望在娱乐行业有所作为的人一样，

sentences.en: Glauber has a dream.
sentences.zh: 格劳伯有一个梦想。

sentences.en: He wants to buy a house.
sentences.zh: 他想买一栋房子。

sentences.en: That's what I've always wanted to do.
sentences.zh: 那是我一直想做的事。

sentences.en: My family has never owned a house.
sentences.zh: 我的家人从来没有拥有过房子。

sentences.en: So I was like, I want to buy a house.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，我想买一栋房子。

sentences.en: And the reason for me buying a house is I wanted to get a bunch of rooms so my artists could come live with me.
sentences.zh: 我买房子的原因是我想多弄几个房间，这样我的艺人就可以搬来和我住在一起。

sentences.en: Like I can get Lambo to come out here and live there and then work on music.
sentences.zh: 比如我可以让Lambo搬到这里住，然后一起做音乐。

sentences.en: Doesn't have to worry about rent.
sentences.zh: 不用担心房租。

sentences.en: Doesn't have to worry about food or anything.
sentences.zh: 不用担心食物或任何事情。

sentences.en: But when he gets to LA, he does not have anywhere near the amount of money he's going to need to do that.
sentences.zh: 但当他到达洛杉矶时，他手里的钱远不足以实现这个目标。

sentences.en: So I'm sleeping on couches.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时睡在沙发上。

sentences.en: I have a friend of mine in Van Nuys.
sentences.zh: 我在范奈斯有一个朋友。

sentences.en: I'm sleeping on his couch.
sentences.zh: 我睡在他的沙发上。

sentences.en: And then I sleep on a couch in West Hills.
sentences.zh: 然后我睡在西山的一张沙发上。

sentences.en: So I actually have screenshots of all of 2017
sentences.zh: 我实际上有2017年全年的截图，

sentences.en: of my bank account because to motivate myself, I changed the name of my bank account to Pro is Broke as Fuck.
sentences.zh: 是我银行账户的截图，因为为了激励自己，我把银行账户的名字改成了“Pro穷得要死”。

sentences.en: And then I had like the little part there and it'd be like a dollar or like 50 cents or like 50 bucks or something like that in my account.
sentences.zh: 然后我账户里只有一点点钱，可能是一美元，或者50美分，或者50美元之类的。

sentences.en: It was crazy.
sentences.zh: 那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: So...
sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: I didn't know you could change the name of your bank account.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你可以更改银行账户的名字。

sentences.en: Yeah, you can.
sentences.zh: 是的，可以。

sentences.en: It's so funny.
sentences.zh: 太搞笑了。

sentences.en: And he starts picking up some freelance video editing gigs.
sentences.zh: 他开始接一些自由职业的视频剪辑工作。

sentences.en: He's making like $1,000 a month.
sentences.zh: 他一个月能赚1000美元左右。

sentences.en: And he eventually gets this break.
sentences.zh: 最终他得到了一个机会。

sentences.en: He gets a job at a startup in LA.
sentences.zh: 他在洛杉矶的一家初创公司找到了一份工作。

sentences.en: They're having him do sort of entry-level video editing.
sentences.zh: 他们让他做一些入门级的视频剪辑工作。

sentences.en: And as he starts getting more experienced and taking on more responsibilities, he eventually starts making a little more money.
sentences.zh: 随着他经验的积累和承担更多的责任，他最终开始赚更多的钱。

sentences.en: All I do is work.
sentences.zh: 我所做的就是工作。

sentences.en: So you're making a little bit more money at that point.
sentences.zh: 所以你当时赚的钱多了一些。

sentences.en: Like, did you change the name of your bank account?
sentences.zh: 那你有没有改掉你的银行账户名字？

sentences.en: Yes, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我改了。

sentences.en: I just went back to what it was for.
sentences.zh: 我把它改回了原来的名字。

sentences.en: But as he's continuing to sort of save up, he really develops like tunnel vision on this goal of buying a house.
sentences.zh: 但随着他继续存钱，他在买房这个目标上变得非常专注。

sentences.en: I do everything in my power to do that.
sentences.zh: 我尽我所能去做这件事。

sentences.en: I'm saving every bit of money that I can.
sentences.zh: 我把能存的每一分钱都存了起来。

sentences.en: Like, my money every month is literally going to bills.
sentences.zh: 我的钱每个月基本上都花在账单上。

sentences.en: My car is a piece of shit.
sentences.zh: 我的车破得要命。

sentences.en: I'm not going out shopping.
sentences.zh: 我不去购物。

sentences.en: I'm not going on vacation.
sentences.zh: 我不去度假。

sentences.en: I'm not going to concerts.
sentences.zh: 我不去听音乐会。

sentences.en: So at the beginning of 2020, he finally has enough money saved up that he thinks he can start looking for a house.
sentences.zh: 所以到2020年初，他终于存够了钱，觉得可以开始看房子了。

sentences.en: But that turns out not to be easy.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明这并不容易。

sentences.en: Like, he just can't find any place that's within his budget.
sentences.zh: 他根本找不到任何在他预算范围内的房子。

sentences.en: So I'm like, I'm going to find a house that's $300,000 because I could do 20% of that.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时想，我要找一栋30万美元的房子，因为我可以支付20%的首付。

sentences.en: So he starts working with a realtor and eventually...
sentences.zh: 于是他开始和房地产经纪人合作，最终……

sentences.en: I find this house in the woods past Pasadena, like up by the mountains, and it's like $350,000.
sentences.zh: 我在帕萨迪纳后面的树林里，靠近山上的地方找到了这栋房子，大概35万美元。

sentences.en: And I'm like, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，那没问题。

sentences.en: At least I'll have a house, right?
sentences.zh: 至少我会有个家，对吧？

sentences.en: That's all I ever wanted.
sentences.zh: 那是我一直想要的。

sentences.en: So he gets really excited.
sentences.zh: 他感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: He can actually afford a down payment on this place.
sentences.zh: 他确实付得起这房子的首付。

sentences.en: So the realtor calls the house, calls me back the next day, and says, oh, they're cash only.
sentences.zh: 结果房地产经纪人第二天给我回电话说，哦，他们只要现金。

sentences.en: You got to pay for the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 你必须全额支付。

sentences.en: And so his dream is dashed again.
sentences.zh: 于是他的梦想再次破灭了。

sentences.en: I'm like, that's it.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，就这样吧。

sentences.en: I can't get a house.
sentences.zh: 我买不到房子。

sentences.en: God doesn't want me to get a house.
sentences.zh: 上帝不想让我拥有房子。

sentences.en: And he ultimately decides, like, maybe this just isn't in the cards for me right now.
sentences.zh: 他最终决定，也许这对我来说现在就是不可能的。

sentences.en: So this is a pretty
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个相当

sentences.en: depressingly familiar version of the American dream, a guy who comes from not very much, works really hard, tries to save up, does save up, and still feels stuck.
sentences.zh: 令人沮丧的、熟悉的美国梦版本：一个出身贫寒的人，工作非常努力，试图存钱，确实存到了钱，但仍然感到被困住了。

sentences.en: Because in a city like Los Angeles, given the economics of trying to buy a home, he is actually stuck.
sentences.zh: 因为在洛杉矶这样的城市，考虑到买房的经济状况，他实际上是被困住了。

sentences.en: The system's just not working for him.
sentences.zh: 这个系统对他来说根本行不通。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This whole classic sense of, like, you work hard, you climb the ladder, you buy a house, you settle down, like, that version of the economy is just not really working for him.
sentences.zh: 那种经典的观念，即你努力工作，步步高升，买房，安家落户，那种经济模式对他来说根本行不通。

sentences.en: But then he figures out that he actually has another option.
sentences.zh: 但随后他发现自己其实还有另一个选择。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
